Q: How do event generations and invalidation prevent stale live-agent results?
A: A live agent can receive a new event while earlier work is still running. Assign generation or version identities to inputs, propagate them through work and verify result ownership before publishing or committing. Cancellation reduces wasted work but may arrive too late, so invalidation at the publication boundary is still required. Define whether events replace prior intent, accumulate or require ordered processing. Effects accepted under an older generation need explicit reconciliation rather than silent abandonment.
Why: A location update makes an earlier recommendation obsolete. A slow earlier lookup may finish last, but the UI must reject that result instead of replacing the newer recommendation solely because it arrived most recently.
Risk: Completion order is not intent order.
Trade: Latest-value processing saves work when replacement semantics are valid; ordered events need a different policy.
Try: Delay the first of two events and prove only the current generation can publish.
